title: Handle a range of customer complaints

lessons.title: Receiving a complaint
lessons.html:
Receiving a complaint

Complaints are part of every business. In the seed industry they often come at a stressful time: a farmer sees poor emergence in a land, a co-op receives the wrong cultivar just before planting, or a delivery arrives late after good rains. Handled well, a complaint can strengthen the relationship. Handled badly, the business loses the customer and its reputation spreads quickly through farmer networks.

Common complaints in seed marketing

  • Poor germination or uneven emergence in the field
  • Wrong cultivar, pack size or quantity delivered
  • Late delivery
  • Damaged or wet bags
  • Crop not performing as promised, for example disease or lodging
  • Invoice or pricing errors
  • Poor service from a representative

How to receive the complaint

  1. Listen fully without interrupting. Let the customer explain.
  2. Stay calm and polite, even if the customer is angry. The anger is about the problem, not you personally.
  3. Show understanding: 'I understand this is serious for you at planting time.'
  4. Ask questions to get the facts: product, lot number on the bag label, invoice number, planting date, conditions, area affected.
  5. Record everything on the complaint form or system.
  6. Explain the next steps and when the customer will hear from you.

What not to do

  • Do not argue or blame the customer.
  • Do not blame colleagues or other departments in front of the customer.
  • Do not promise compensation before the complaint has been investigated, unless you have authority.
  • Do not ignore the complaint or delay without explanation.

Keep the bag labels and a sample of the seed if the customer still has it. These are vital evidence for the laboratory.

lessons.title: Investigating and resolving complaints
lessons.html:
Investigating and resolving complaints

Once a complaint is recorded, it must be investigated fairly and resolved within a reasonable time. Different types of complaints need different actions.

Investigating

ComplaintHow to investigate
Poor emergenceField visit; check planting depth, soil moisture, crusting, insects, herbicide damage; retest the retained lot sample for germination
Wrong product deliveredCheck order, picking list and delivery note
Late deliveryCheck dispatch records and transport
Pricing errorCheck price list, quote and invoice

Field complaints need technical skill. Poor emergence is often caused by planting conditions, such as planting too deep into dry soil or soil crusting after heavy rain, rather than by the seed. The retained sample result helps show whether the seed lot was at fault. Explain findings to the customer with evidence, respectfully.

Resolving

  • If the business is at fault, accept responsibility and offer a fair solution within company policy: replacement seed, credit, refund or corrected delivery.
  • If the cause is outside the business's control, explain clearly, share the evidence and give advice to avoid the problem next time.
  • Escalate to a manager when the complaint is beyond your authority or involves large claims or legal matters.
  • Agree the solution with the customer and confirm it in writing.

Follow-up

Phone the customer after the solution was delivered to check they are satisfied. Close the complaint in the system with the outcome.

Learning from complaints

Review complaint records regularly. Many complaints about one lot may mean a quality problem; many delivery complaints may mean a transport problem. Report trends to management so causes can be fixed.

The Consumer Protection Act gives consumers rights to fair treatment and safe, good-quality goods. Many large farm businesses fall outside its scope, but treating every customer fairly is good business.

Key points

  • Listen, stay calm, get the facts and record the complaint.
  • Keep bag labels and seed samples as evidence.
  • Investigate fairly; poor emergence often has field causes.
  • Resolve within policy and escalate when beyond your authority.
  • Follow up and use complaint trends to improve.
